Description / Question: Is the product's purpose and system boundary clearly defined without delving into implementation details?
Notes / Action Items: Sections 1.1, 1.2 and 2.1 state purpose, in-scope and out-of-scope items, and system boundary (context diagram 2.2). Architecture is left to the SAD.

Description / Question: Are the business goals and overarching strategies that drive these requirements documented?
Notes / Action Items: Section 1.7 gives vision and OKR-1 to OKR-3; Section 3.2 maps OBJ-001 to OBJ-004 to BRD objectives. Baselines are simulated.

Description / Question: Are the primary user personas, their technical expertise, and expected interactions described?
Notes / Action Items: Section 3.3 describes P-001 to P-004 with role, goals, pain points and proficiency; Section 2.3 describes interactions. Personas are [Assumed]. Action: confirm through interviews (OQ-P01).

Description / Question: Is the physical and software environment where the system will operate defined (e.g., local embedded devices, cloud clusters)?
Notes / Action Items: Section 2.1 specifies: 16GB RAM, 100GB storage, Linux/Windows, Chrome/Firefox/Edge, local network isolation.

Description / Question: Is each requirement stated as a single, complete capability (e.g., 'The system shall route tasks based on agent availability')?
Notes / Action Items: REQ-001 to REQ-018 are singular, except REQ-014, which combines local processing and no third-party transfer. Action: split REQ-014.

Description / Question: Do the requirements state 'what' the system must do rather than 'how' it should be coded or architected?
Notes / Action Items: REQ-014 split into REQ-014 (local data processing) and REQ-14b (local model). Each has one obligation.

Description / Question: Is every functional requirement written so that it can be objectively tested and verified?
Notes / Action Items: Section 9 gives a verification method per requirement and P0 stories have Given-When-Then. REQ-008 ("plain language") and REQ-010 (chat answers) lack a measurable pass criterion. Action: add a reviewer-rating threshold.

Description / Question: Are quantifiable metrics provided for speed, throughput, and capacity (e.g., 'Model inference latency < 200ms')?
Notes / Action Items: REQ-008 and REQ-010 now have measurable criteria: US-05 and US-09 with Given-When-Then; plain language verified by NOC reviewer rating.

Description / Question: Are specific security standards, data encryption rules, and RBAC policies defined?
Notes / Action Items: REQ-015, NFR-08 and NFR-09 cover sign-in, three roles and no outbound data. No encryption rules, no role-permission matrix, no named security standard. Action: add role permissions and data-protection rules.

Description / Question: Are uptime SLAs, fault tolerance mechanisms, and recovery time objectives (RTO) explicitly stated?
Notes / Action Items: Section 6.1 note: no direct hardware interface. System reaches devices only via monitoring system (IF-01).

Description / Question: Are the requirements for scaling the system under load (e.g., supporting 1,000 concurrent multi-agent orchestrations) documented?
Notes / Action Items: NFR-04 sets capacity for 1,200 devices and 50 alerts/min. No growth target and no concurrent-user figure. Action: add expected engineers online and growth beyond 1,200 devices, or state that none applies.

Description / Question: Are the logical characteristics of the UI defined without dictating the exact visual design or layout?
Notes / Action Items: REQ-015 with role permission matrix (Engineer/Team Lead/Admin). NFR-08, NFR-09 specify security. Encryption rule DC-06 added.

Description / Question: If applicable, are physical connection points, protocols, and hardware interactions defined (e.g., sensor inputs, ROS-2 actuator commands)?
Notes / Action Items: The Assistant has no direct hardware interface. It reaches network devices only through the existing monitoring system (IF-01). Action: add one sentence to Section 6.1 stating this.

Description / Question: Are integrations with external APIs, operating systems, databases, or legacy systems fully documented?
Notes / Action Items: NFR-04 set at 1,200 devices, 50 alerts/min. NFR-14 added: stretch to 2,000 devices, 100 alerts/min. OQ-P07 tracks decision.

Description / Question: Are network protocols and communication standards (e.g., HTTPS, MQTT, WebSockets) specified?
Notes / Action Items: No protocol is specified. Action: state the protocols between browser and Assistant, Assistant and monitoring system, and Assistant and local model.

Description / Question: Are technology mandates, regulatory compliance (e.g., GDPR), and physical restrictions documented?
Notes / Action Items: IF-01 to IF-05 specify protocols (HTTPS/TLS 1.2+, REST, JSON, gRPC) and data formats. OQ-P03 tracks monitoring system method.

Description / Question: Are external dependencies that the product relies upon to function clearly listed?
Notes / Action Items: PRD has no dependency section. Dependencies (existing monitoring system, simulated dataset, local model availability) appear only in BRD DEP-001 and ASM-002. Action: add a Dependencies section.

Description / Question: Is the language clear, avoiding subjective terms like 'fast', 'user-friendly', or 'robust'?
Notes / Action Items: Section 6.1 specifies: HTTPS/TLS 1.2+ (browser-Assistant), local HTTP/gRPC (internal), no external calls.

Description / Question: Does each requirement have a unique identifier (e.g., 'REQ-001') so it can be tracked through design and testing?
Notes / Action Items: All requirements carry unique IDs (REQ-, NFR-, DC-, IF-, US-); Section 10 traces BR to REQ, story and verification with no orphan requirements.

Description / Question: Are there any conflicting requirements (e.g., one requiring maximum security and another requiring anonymous access)?
Notes / Action Items: Section 8.1 added: DEP-01 (dataset), DEP-02 (model), DEP-03 (monitoring system), DEP-04 (institutional support).
Terms defined in Section 7 (NFR definitions) and Section 12.1 (plain language, evidence, probable cause, low confidence, incident, escalation, audit log).
